definition: Laboratory automation is a multi-disciplinary strategy to research, develop, optimize and capitalize on technologies in the laboratory that enable new and improved processes.
details: Laboratory automation professionals are academic, commercial and government researchers, scientists and engineers who conduct research and develop new technologies to increase productivity, elevate experimental data quality, reduce lab process cycle times, or enable experimentation that otherwise would be impossible. The most widely known application of laboratory automation technology is laboratory robotics. More generally, the field of laboratory automation comprises many different automated laboratory instruments, devices (the most common being autosamplers), software algorithms, and methodologies used to enable, expedite and increase the efficiency and effectiveness of scientific research in laboratories. The application of technology in today's laboratories is required to achieve timely progress and remain competitive. Laboratories devoted to activities such as high-throughput screening, combinatorial chemistry, automated clinical and analytical testing, diagnostics, large-scale biorepositories, and many others, would not exist without advancements in laboratory automation. explainer.lead: Laboratory automation is a multi-disciplinary strategy to research, develop and optimize lab technologies for new and improved processes. It matters because it raises throughput and data quality and enables experiments that would otherwise be impossible.

tiers.eli5: It is fitting a lab with machines and smart workflows so experiments run faster, more consistently, and sometimes in ways people could not do by hand.
tiers.practitioner: Academic, commercial and government scientists apply it to cut process cycle times and boost productivity. A pitfall is treating automation as plug-and-play; processes must be redesigned around the automated steps.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined broadly, laboratory automation covers many automated lab technologies, with laboratory robotics as its best-known application. Benefits cited include higher productivity, better experimental data quality, and reduced cycle times.

explainer.example: A lab redesigns a repetitive assay pipeline so instruments and software handle sample handling, shortening cycle time and improving data consistency.
